chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Abi Basir, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who killed another man intentionally, then the killer fled and could not be apprehended. He said: “If he has property, the blood-money is taken from his property; otherwise, then from the nearest relatives and then the next nearest, because the blood of a Muslim man is not to be left without redress.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: blood-money; the prescribed financial compensation for unlawful killing
key_terms.الْأَقْرَبِ: the nearest relative; indicating closest kin in financial liability
key_terms.الْقَاتِلُ: the killer; the person who committed the murder
key_terms.دَمُ امْرِئٍ مُسْلِمٍ: the blood of a Muslim person; meaning a protected life whose right cannot be nullified
key_terms.مَالٌ: property or wealth belonging to the killer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if an intentional killer escapes and cannot be caught?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning intentional killing when the murderer escapes and cannot be seized. It establishes that the diyah is taken from the killer's wealth, and if that is unavailable, liability passes to the nearest kin, affirming that the blood of a Muslim cannot be rendered void.
